key_insight: The paper argues that AI safety needs new mathematics across multiple fields to make AI systems legible, steerable, and cooperative with humans.
engineering_relevance: For engineering teams, it highlights where formal methods from logic, probability, algebra, and analysis may support safer model design, interpretability, and training stability.
method: Map AI safety problems to core mathematical areas: cooperation via logic/game theory, agency via probability, features via algebra/representation theory, and training/generalization via analysis/geometry.
Use field-specific open problems as entry points for mathematicians to contribute directly to AI safety.
Organize the agenda by mathematical discipline to connect theory with practical safety challenges.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a position/invitation piece rather than an experimental study, so its support is conceptual and framed by open problems instead of empirical evaluation.
watch_item: The proposed connections are broad and promising, but translating abstract mathematics into deployable safety mechanisms may be slow and domain-dependent.
paper_title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians
